description: Ephemeral Workspaces, durable shared history. LayerFS gives every agent a complete, writable filesystem Workspace over shared committed history, without copying the base. Agents work in parallel, commit what changed as deduplicated checkpoints, then branch, rewind or merge. Try it with LayerFS × DSH.
summary: LayerFS puts a content-addressed, copy-on-write filesystem under a fleet of agents: each one mounts a full writable workspace over shared committed history, does its work, commits only the deltas, and unmounts, so parallel sessions branch and merge like git branches but at the block level. The storage math is the part that sold me—157 snapshots of a real project in 100 MB, roughly 20× tighter than Btrfs plus zstd—which means "spin up fifty agent workspaces" stops being a disk and I/O problem. For PenguPool this is the layer I keep hand-rolling: right now each routed session in VS Code still gets its own scratch directory, and LayerFS would let them share one durable, rewindable history while staying ephemeral enough that a killed agent leaves nothing behind (the current build is disposable-profile only, so it is not your backup, but for agent scratch state it is exactly right).
